Unlike traditional link prediction, which focuses primarily on predicting links using node attributes and current topology, TLP requires models that capture complex temporal and spatial network dynamics. This presents the challenging task of forecasting future link formation based on both historical and current network states. Representation Methods Temporal graphs can be described using two distinct approaches for the time dimension: Discrete-time Dynamic Graphs (DTDG): A DTDG simplifies a temporal network into a sequence of timestamped snapshots, converting the continuous temporal space into discrete timestamps. This allows dynamic graphs to be represented in a static, analysable format, though some information may be lost between snapshots during discretisation. Continuous-time Dynamic Graphs (CTDG): This method abstains from discretising the time dimension. Instead, it characterises the presence of all elements independently within a continuous temporal space, preserving the inherent temporal continuity of temporal networks.
